source_tamil_lines: வீடுவாசல் மாடு மனை மக்கள் சுற்றம் போலாலும்
english_lines: Public welfare — always public welfare,
A most sacred act that guards the body of fame,
Public welfare — always public welfare,
House, threshold, cattle, home, people and kin though there may be,
Country — our country, good country — saying 'country',
It is the sacrifice we all make together,
(Public welfare)
notes: `புகழ் உடல்` is retained as the striking `body of fame` image rather than reduced to reputation.
The household-to-country accumulation is preserved line by line rather than summarized as patriotism.

source_tamil_lines: உருப்படா மனிதனுக்குயிர் கொடுக்கும் மருந்து - நல்ல மருந்து
english_lines: Fit for nothing in the country,
Doing no work at all in the house — into the body,
As into a cage, stuffing food and living,
A medicine that gives life to the useless man — a good medicine.
notes: The `உடல் / கூட்டில்` sequence is kept as a body-as-cage image instead of smoothed into merely eating idly.
The ridicule of the idle man remains direct.

english_lines: The pandaaram who sleeps on the front veranda,
The paradesi bearing the sacred begging bowl,
The Tirupati Govinda rolling in the street — Govinda, Govinda,
A medicine that gives life to this lazy walking corpse,
(Public welfare)
notes: `பண்டாரம்`, `பரதேசி`, and `கோவிந்தா` retain their culture-bearing force by transliteration/title rather than being collapsed into generic beggars.
`நடைபிணம்` remains the harsh concrete `walking corpse` image.

source_tamil_lines: கச்சிதமாய் அகற்றிவிடும் கைகண்ட மருந்து - நல்ல மருந்து
english_lines: The lines that fall upon the forehead,
The lines of old age,
The evils that grow in the mind,
A proven medicine that removes them precisely — a good medicine,
Worship at the temple of knowledge,
The culture of the working comrade,
Let us live, let us live, with love along the path of virtue,
A medicine that gives light to these higher duties,
(Public welfare)
notes: `அறிவுக்கோயில்` remains the `temple of knowledge`, and `உழைக்கும் தோழர்` remains the explicitly labour-oriented `working comrade`.
`கைகண்ட மருந்து` is rendered as a proven medicine; the extended medicine metaphor is preserved across all stanzas.

translator_notes: The song treats public welfare as medicine for idleness, age, intellectual harm and civic duty; the repeated medicinal metaphor and social satire remain intact.
PDF 62–63 provenance remains attached to one translation record.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
